essay_snippets.150_word_bio: Hrishiv Khatiwala is a rising junior at Green Hope High School in Cary, NC, with a GPA of 4.696 (weighted) and a class rank of 7 out of 652. He co-founded a nationally ranked rocketry team that placed 2nd among 1,001 teams, co-founded a VEX Robotics team invited to the U.S. Open (top 150 worldwide), and holds the 2025 NC State Record in Science Olympiad's Helicopter event. He has conducted research at both Duke University (MATLAB-based 3D scaffold analysis) and NC State University (ML models for hurricane tracking), and has a published paper on Zenodo. He is concurrently enrolled at Wake Technical Community College (4.0 GPA). Beyond STEM, he co-founded a Books for Africa chapter that shipped $85,000 in educational materials to Kenya and Tanzania.
essay_snippets.why_stem: My interest in STEM started with a rubber-band-powered balsa airplane and deepened through Science Olympiad, where I optimized flight mechanics and eventually set a NC State Record. Competing in the American Rocketry Challenge pushed me further — I built AI altitude prediction models and fabricated custom 3D-printed fins, reducing prediction error to under 10 feet. Working in real research labs at Duke and NC State showed me that the questions that matter most sit at the intersection of disciplines: materials science, machine learning, and atmospheric modeling. I want to keep working at those intersections.
essay_snippets.leadership: I have co-founded two competitive STEM teams from scratch — a rocketry team that reached the national finals and a robotics team that earned a worldwide invitation. In both cases, I not only built the technical systems but recruited teammates, secured funding through grants, and represented the team to industry professionals and judges. Leadership, to me, means making the people around you more capable.
essay_snippets.community_impact: Through co-founding a Books for Africa chapter, I mobilized over 1,400 community members to collect 10,000+ books and ship $85,000 in educational materials to rural Kenya and Tanzania. Through Robotics for All, I helped develop curriculum that reached 5,000+ students across the country. And through 350+ hours at Science of the Soul Study, I have learned that sustained, unglamorous service matters more than single-event heroics.
